subject: Request: Temporary analytics processor (TelemetryX) — evidence & rollback plan
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finbridge.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, procurement <procurement@finbridge.com>
Date: 2028-07-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Request: add TelemetryX as temporary analytics processor for pilot

Hi Irene / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re planning a short pilot for our EU telemetry pipeline and would like to contract TelemetryX as a temporary analytics processor for a 6-week window (pilot start targeted 2028-07-25). Before we can proceed, our privacy/compliance team needs: 

- a signed DPA addendum or written confirmation that TelemetryX will be added as a subprocessor
- a short dataflow diagram showing exactly which telemetry elements will be delivered to TelemetryX and whether PII is excluded
- evidence of TelemetryX’s SOC 2 / security posture (or equivalent attestations)
- an internal rollback/stop-processing plan in the event of an incident

Can Redwood provide a timeline for review and the minimal evidence packet we should expect? We can also share a short supplier questionnaire if that helps.

Attaching a short internal checklist on our side (see separate message). Happy to set a 30-minute sync if easier — pref 2028-07-15 morning CEST.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Privacy & Compliance
FinBridge Payments

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Request: add TelemetryX as temporary analytics processor for pilot

Thanks, Elena — and great to meet you on the demo. We can support a temporary processor for the pilot but need to validate a handful of items before giving formal approval. I’ve attached Redwood’s standard processor evidence checklist to make this as predictable as possible.

Quick answers up front: 
- Review timeline: we typically complete an evidence review + legal DPA addendum in 7-10 business days for temporary processors if vendor evidence is complete.
- Rollback/stop-processing: we will require a documented stop-processing playbook that includes (a) immediate traffic cut, (b) token/key rotations, and (c) data deletion verification from TelemetryX. We can provide a template.
- Data minimization: if FinBridge can ensure telemetry payloads exclude any customer identifiers (or pseudonymize before send), that will reduce our controls and speed approval.

Next steps (proposed):
1) FinBridge shares TelemetryX evidence (SOC2 report, encryption attestations, IP allowlist, contact for audits).
2) TelemetryX provides a short dataflow SVG/diagram and confirms retention periods.
3) Redwood Legal prepares a DPA addendum draft for temporary subprocessor binding.
4) Security performs a 72-hour evidence review window once we have docs; procurement coordinates signing.

I’ve attached the checklist and a blank rollback template. If you can send TelemetryX’s contact we’ll ping them directly to avoid back-and-forth.

Thanks — I’ll be your point of contact here.

—
Irene Choi
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[attachment: processor_evidence_checklist.pdf (pdf)]

Internal notes / draft risk summary below — forwarding so Jordan can slot this into the procurement/ops timeline.

Quoted: 
> Irene: We can support a temporary processor for the pilot but need to validate a handful of items before giving formal approval. I’ve attached Redwood’s standard processor evidence checklist to make this as predictable as possible.

Risk summary (initial, high-level):
- Data residency: TelemetryX has EU infrastructure (good) but their support team is in APAC — need confirmation that live support does not require export of telemetry payloads.
- Sensitive tokens: confirm that no customer auth tokens are forwarded; if present, require token redaction step.
- Retention & deletion: require a verified deletion API and deletion certificate post-pilot.

Procurement/legal asks: please draft a DPA addendum that: 
- limits TelemetryX to specified telemetry types and retention <= 30 days for the pilot
- includes the stop-processing playbook as an annex
- includes audit rights limited to evidence review for the pilot period only

Timeline suggestion: 
- 2028-07-14: collect vendor evidence and dataflow (FinBridge/TelemetryX)
- 2028-07-17: security evidence review complete (72-hour window)
- 2028-07-18: DPA addendum ready for signature (procurement to circulate)
- 2028-07-25: pilot start (conditional on sign-off)

Attaching a quick dataflow sketch (will formalize once we get TelemetryX diagram).
